source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"An unexplained glucose rise can be observed for several hours before checking the infusion set, because brief pump interruptions rarely cause ketosis.","B":"Infusion-set dislodgement or occlusion can interrupt rapid-acting insulin delivery and lead to ketosis or DKA, so pump problems must be recognized and managed early.","C":"Once pump settings are stable, infusion-set problems are unlikely to alter glucose rapidly because the body maintains a large depot of long-acting insulin.","D":"Pump users can reduce glucose monitoring after the first week of therapy because device malfunction is usually detected before meaningful hyperglycemia or ketosis develops."}}
source_row.rationale: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026 state that infusion-set dislodgement and occlusion place pump users at risk for ketosis and DKA and must be recognized and managed early; pump education includes troubleshooting. Option B reflects that risk. Option A delays troubleshooting. Option C incorrectly assumes a protective long-acting insulin depot. Option D inappropriately reduces monitoring despite the possibility of device interruption.
source_row.source_detail: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, Section 7 Diabetes Technology — Complications and Challenges of Infusing Insulin: infusion-set dislodgement and occlusion can interrupt insulin delivery, creating risk for ketosis/DKA, and must be recognized and managed early; pump education includes troubleshooting. FDA 2026 insulin-pump recall data independently corroborate that insulin under-delivery can cause severe hyperglycemia and DKA. Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, Diabetes Care 49(Suppl 1), published 2025-12-08 for 2026; current annual ADA guideline and FDA 2026 device safety data rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: medication administration, calculations, adverse effects/interactions, monitoring and client teaching. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
